subject: Priority request: HelioBank tenant-aware routing shim
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Priority request: HelioBank tenant-aware routing shim

Team —

HelioBank (contact: Samira Khan) surfaced a hard requirement in procurement: they need tenant-level routing isolation for PCI-sensitive traffic so tokenized requests never share inference workers with non-PCI tenants. This is a gating item for a ~7-figure committed ARR deal (see attached MAA/proforma).

Ask: can Eng/Product prioritize a small "tenant-aware routing shim" that will allow us to steer PCI-labeled requests to a separate routing path (same model binary but isolated worker pool + config) for initial rollout? They don't require a full tenant isolation product — this is a stop-gap feature to unblock procurement and the legal team.

Constraints / context:
- Expected sustained QPS: 120 rps during peak, burst to 250 rps.
- Latency SLO must remain within our p95 target for the dedicated pool.
- Initial scope: routing tag + simple affinity to pool, config toggle in Console, and a migration plan. No KV-cache changes in MVP.
- Timeline ask from customer: deployment in their US region by end of June (6 weeks).

I copied Ben to evaluate business tradeoffs. Marissa: I'll coordinate a short call with Samira to sync on acceptance criteria. Dev: would appreciate an early read on feasibility and an estimate (engineering effort + any product gating needed).

Attachments: HelioBank_MAA_proforma_v2.pdf, heliobank-routing-requirements.xlsx

Thanks,
Kimberly
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Priority request: HelioBank tenant-aware routing shim

Kimberly —

Thanks for the clear brief and attachments (reviewed the routing requirements spreadsheet). High-level thoughts: this is achievable as a scoped engineering effort if we accept some limitations in the MVP. Key questions that change effort:

1) Strict isolation vs affinity: do we need absolute non-co residency (no co-located KV/cache) or just routing to a separate worker pool? Absolute isolation (no shared cache) is significantly heavier.
2) Autoscaling policy for the dedicated pool: will HelioBank accept a reserved min capacity (e.g., 2x expected baseline) while we validate? That reduces complexity.
3) Observability/traceability: we should include route-level traces and a per-tenant audit flag for SOC/PCI evidence — small effort but important for procurement.

Rough estimate (very rough):
- Routing tag + routing table + Console toggle: 1.5 engineer-weeks
- Pool affinity + autoscale policy config: 1.5 engineer-weeks
- Basic trace/audit hooks & docs: 1 engineer-week
Total: ~4 engineer-weeks (1 engineer full-time ~4 weeks) to get a safe MVP into staging, plus 1 week for validation and runbook. If we deprioritize a feature in the current sprint we could meet the ~6-week customer window, otherwise it will slip.

Tradeoffs: we will not address KV-cache eviction/replication for the MVP; that would be a follow-up if HelioBank needs strict cryptographic separation. Also need Security to sign off on the audit evidence.

Action items I need from Sales:
- Confirm whether "no co-residency at all" is required or "dedicated pool affinity" suffices.
- Provide expected QPS over a 24h period (not just peak) and any SLA penalties in the contract we must be aware of.

I'll hold a quick sync with Marissa/Ben if you want to walk through the proposed design.

—Dev
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-13T15:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Priority request: HelioBank tenant-aware routing shim

Marissa / Dev / Kimberly —

I've reviewed the ask and the proposed scope. Product is willing to carve out a single scoped ticket in the June sprint for a "tenant-aware routing shim" with the constraints Dev laid out, provided we accept the following acceptance criteria:

1) Routing tag + routing table implemented and feature-flagged in Console.
2) Dedicated worker pool affinity with a documented autoscaling profile and a recommended reserved-min setting.
3) Trace-level logging for routed requests stored for 90 days and an audit export workflow for procurement.
4) No changes to model binaries or KV-cache policy in MVP. Any cache separation request will be considered in a follow-up.

We will tag the ticket as: product-priority:deal (HLB-2027-004) and track completion in the sprint board. Dev — please submit a scoped PRD (1pager) and a list of acceptance tests by EOD Monday so we can lock scope in the sprint planning meeting.

Kimberly / Marissa — please confirm commercial terms (reserved capacity sizing + acceptance window) so we can include the right language in the amendment.

Ben Carter
Head of Product, Inference Platform
Redwood Inference
